parsed_output.analysis: The specification requires a single composite state Collision_Avoidance_Active_Mode that is entered as a whole when a possible frontend, rear-end or pedestrian collision is detected, and that composite contains three orthogonal regions that can be active concurrently with different collision-avoidance controls. The PlantUML model defines Collision_Avoidance_Active_Mode with three -- separated partitions, each containing a single state F/R/P with its own internal [*] -> state transition labelled “collision detected” and state -> [*] labelled “Collision avoided”. There is no external entry/exit to the composite state, the entry conditions for the regions are generic and identical, and each region only contains one leaf state.

issues.issue: Composite sub-machine has no activation entry
issues.reason: Specification 2 says the sub-machine becomes active when a possible frontend collision, rear-end collision or collision with pedestrian is detected. The model contains no transition into Collision_Avoidance_Active_Mode from outside; activation is only modelled as internal [*] -> F/R/P transitions.
issues.where: state Collision_Avoidance_Active_Mode definition – no incoming transition to the composite

issues.issue: Region entry triggers are generic and not type-specific
issues.reason: Specification requires activation on a possible frontend collision, rear-end collision or pedestrian collision. The model uses the same generic label “collision detected” for all three regions, so a single detection event would be interpreted as triggering all three regions and there is no distinction between frontend, rear-end and pedestrian detections.
issues.where: [*] --> F : collision detected, [*] --> R : collision detected, [*] --> P : collision detected

issues.issue: Entry condition is modelled per region instead of per composite
issues.reason: Specification 2 states the sub-machine as a whole becomes active on detection, and Specification 3 states the orthogonal regions allow concurrent activation of different controls once the mode is active. The model ties the detection trigger to the internal initial transition of each region, implying three independent activations rather than one composite activation followed by concurrent region activation.
issues.where: Each of the three -- partitions has its own [*] --> state transition with the detection trigger

issues.issue: No modelling of concurrent different collision avoidance controls
issues.reason: Specification 3 requires orthogonal regions of the active mode to allow for concurrent activation of different collision avoidance controls. The model provides only one leaf state per region and no distinct control states/actions, so concurrent, differentiated controls are not represented.
issues.where: Regions F, R, P each contain a single state “Frontend collision”, “Rear-end collision”, “Collision with pedestrian” with only Collision avoided exit

system_prompt:
You are an experienced control-systems engineer reviewing a state machine model against the natural-language specification it was built from.

You are given two things, both complete and unmodified:
  1. The natural-language specification.
  2. A state machine model written in PlantUML.

Your task: identify the places where the model does not conform to the specification. Read the specification in full first, then read the model in full, then report what you find.

Report as many or as few issues as you actually find, and organize them however you judge best. For each issue, state what the non-conformance is, which part of the model it concerns, and why you consider it a non-conformance.

Write your findings in en-US. Return only the requested structured response.
user_prompt:
## Natural-language specification

1. There are three region in this diagram 
2. This sub-machine becomes active when a possible frontend collision, rear-end collision or collision with pedestrian is detected. 
3. The orthogonal regions of the active mode of collision avoidance allow for concurrent activation different of collision avoidance controls.

## State machine model (PlantUML)

@startuml
state Collision_Avoidance_Active_Mode {
--
[*] --> F : collision detected
state "Frontend collision" as F
F --> [*] : Collision avoided

--
[*] --> R : collision detected
state "Rear-end collision" as R
R --> [*] : Collision avoided

--
[*] --> P : collision detected
state "Collision with pedestrian" as P
P --> [*] : Collision avoided
}
@enduml
